Q: I want to run Forge Neo on Google Colabratoly A:

The OP omits many details, such as the contents of launch.py, and I cannot reproduce that error. I did mkdir to create a new directory, cd'd into it, and then executed the following commands on MacOS Tahoe 26.3 (which is not linux).

uv add gradio-rangeslider protobuf tensorflow tf-keras

Q: How to fix "Unable to process template language expressions for action 'Condition_9' at line '0' and column '0'" error on PowerAutomate A:

I believe the answer is either to remove the possibility for any values to come in other than 0-10 (such as empty values) or to preformat the values as integers so you don't need to change them.

Things to consider: Is this happening all of the time or only for some responses? If the numbers are indeed coming in as a string, it sounds like the responses aren't always coming in as numbers, which leads me to believe it's coming in as something other than a number sometimes such as an empty value. Does it allow for anything besides 0-10 to be passed through? Is the value somewhere that someone can pass it up and not supply a value?

Q: include_path fatal error xampp A:

This happened to me once, My problem was that i had extracted an old project into the xampp folder. This old project included an .htaccess file which was messing with everything within the xampp folder. The solution was to delete the .htaccess file. I hope this helps someone.

Q: Using FTD2XX_NET managed .NET wrapper class to read real time temperature data A:

You cannot get available bytes from calling FtdiWrapper.GetRxBytesAvailable. You need to call FtdiWrapper.Read in a loop until you get your expected bytes, then jump out the loop.

Q: C++: why is iter++->empty() legal? A:

So, it seems like c++ requires compilers to parse expressions in a more complex way than just parenthesizing based on precedence and associativity. Is that right? If there is an easy way to explain how this actually happens, I would like to know about it.

I responded to a similar question here. If you look into the grammar in the C++11 ISO Standard draft you can generate the parse tree pretty easily:

postfix-expression:
    primary-expression
    postfix-expression ()
    postfix-expression -> id-expression
    postfix-expression ++

primary-expression:
    id-expression

                                      POSTFIX-EXPRESSION
                                       |               |
                            POSTFIX-EXPRESSION         ()
                            |      |         |
             POSTFIX-EXPRESSION    ->    ID_EXPRESSION
              |              |               |  
     POSTFIX-EXPRESSION      ++            empty
              |
      PRIMARY_EXPRESSION
              |
        ID_EXPRESSION
              |
             iter

i.e.

                             POSTFIX-EXPRESSION
                              |              |
                   POSTFIX-EXPRESSION        ()
                   |      |         |
    POSTFIX-EXPRESSION    ->        empty
       |            | 
      iter         ++

Q: I want to combine images of different sizes. (Image Magick) A:

In Imagemagick 6, you would need to get the height of image 1 first in a separate command. For example on a Unix-based system:

ht=`convert image1.png -format "%h" info:`
convert image1.png \( image2.png -resize x${ht} \) +append result.png

In Imagemagick 7, you can do it all in one command line:

magick image1.png -set option:ht "%h" \( image2.png -resize "x%[ht]" \) +append result.png

Example:

Input

ht=`convert monet2.jpg -format "%h" info:`
convert monet2.jpg \( zelda1.jpg -resize x${ht} \) +append result.png
